overview.summary:
This module provides shared PayPal integration utilities used by server-side functions. It centralizes PayPal configuration and HTTP interactions: determining the API base URL, confirming configuration is present, computing token reuse lifetime, obtaining an OAuth2 client-credentials access token, and performing a lightweight local check of PayPal signature headers. The module also exposes higher-level operations for creating subscriptions (returning the approval URL for user redirection), verifying webhook signatures using PayPal's verify-webhook-signature API, and looking up a captured payment (sale) to extract the associated subscription and amount.

All network-facing operations that interact with PayPal’s APIs are implemented as async functions. The file separates simple helpers (base URL, configuration check, token lifetime calculation, and a plausibility check for headers) from operations that perform remote calls (token fetch, subscription creation, webhook verification, and sale retrieval), so callers can compose these primitives as needed for webhooks and subscription flows.

overview.summary:
This TypeScript module contains small, test-focused helpers and a set of unit tests for PayPal-related verification and token lifetime logic. It imports plausiblePaypalSignature and tokenLifetimeS from a local paypal.ts module and defines two module-level functions, eq and headers, which are used by the test registrations. The file registers three Deno.test cases that exercise plausiblePaypalSignature behavior for accepted and refused signatures and tokenLifetimeS behavior for reuse and expiry edge cases.

The file is organized around tests: two tests validate the acceptable PayPal certificate hostnames and refusal behavior for other hosts, and a third test validates token lifetime handling (when tokens are reused and when they are considered unknown). The module-level helper functions support these test cases without exposing additional exported functionality beyond what is imported from the local paypal.ts module.

overview.summary:
This SQL file applies security-hardening measures and runtime guards for the SmartBudget database. It introduces atomic usage reservation and release functions (reserve_usage and release_usage) that serialize per-user usage checks with advisory locks, enforce per-user and platform-wide monthly and lifetime limits for AI requests and OCR scans, and update corresponding monthly and lifetime usage tables. The file also restricts direct client manipulation of profile data, ensures webhook ordering by adding a provider event timestamp column to subscriptions, and enforces a maximum size for cloud backup payloads via a table check constraint.

In addition to the procedural logic, the script adjusts privileges so only the Edge Functions (service_role) can execute the usage reservation/release functions, limits insert/update/delete rights on profiles for anonymous/authenticated roles while granting a specific subset of update columns to authenticated users, and creates supporting indexes for monthly usage aggregates. These changes are intended to be safe to re-run and to be applied after the other schema and function definitions are in place.

overview.summary: This SQL file is a consolidated, single-shot database setup for the SmartBudget application intended to run in the Supabase SQL editor. It begins a transaction and applies a sequence of schema and data changes (assembled from multiple component SQL files) to create foundational database objects: extensions, reference tables for currencies and exchange rates, domain tables such as user profiles and taxonomy tables, and seeded reference data for supported currencies. The script uses defensive, idempotent constructs (CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS, ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE) to allow safe re-application and to ensure required reference rows exist before runtime operations like profile creation. The file also documents design decisions relevant to the schema (money stored as integer minor units, row-level security for user-owned tables) and includes indexes and defaults for operational correctness.

overview.summary:
This SQL file implements an automated suite of access-control tests that run against a Supabase-style schema. It seeds test accounts and sample rows for transactions, backups, subscriptions, entitlements, usage, and related billing and logging tables, then switches to an authenticated role with a configured JWT subject to simulate a signed-in user. A temporary results table and a PL/pgSQL helper function (pg_temp.attempt) are created to execute statements, capture whether each attempt succeeded or was denied, and record PASS/FAIL outcomes along with brief diagnostics.

The remainder of the file runs many individual test cases by invoking the helper, exercising reads, writes, updates, and deletes across user-scoped and global tables to verify row-level security and permission constraints. Tests include attempts to access or modify other users' data, create or change subscriptions and entitlements, reset usage counters, call resource-reservation functions, and inspect billing and coupon data; each attempt expects either a denied result or a specific number of affected rows and is recorded in the temporary results table.

overview.summary:
This TypeScript test module contains a collection of utility and test helper functions used for exercising payment and subscription-related behavior in the Supabase test harness. It imports a set of harness utilities and mocks (including check, db, finish, load, model, outbound, paypal, paypalHeaders, paypalSub, PRICES, whop, whopCheckouts, whopHeaders, whopMem, whopMemberships) and exposes helpers for invoking and inspecting simulated calls, building request payloads, encoding data, generating JWTs, scanning and manipulating dates, and performing basic create/delete operations against the test environment. Several functions are asynchronous, indicating integration with async test flows, and the module also explicitly sets and deletes various environment variables (for example OCR_TIMEOUT_MS, AI_TIMEOUT_MS, FOUNDING_OFFER_ENDS_AT, PAYPAL_API_URL, WHOP_API_URL, and PAY_TEST_USER_IDS) to configure the test runtime.

The module-level functions include straightforward utilities such as calls, last, lastPlan, scan, nextMonth, before, stuckUsed, ask, askBody, cfg, b64, jwt and D, together with async routines checkout, yearly and del. These functions collectively support constructing test requests, encoding and signing payloads, manipulating time-related test state, and driving checkout/subscription test scenarios against mocked PayPal and Whop endpoints configured by the harness imports and environment variable adjustments.
